claims.statement: The Foo Valley Municipal Utility confirmed that on 14 July 2025 the Lower Basin treatment works dosed chlorine at four times the permitted level for roughly three hours.

sources.title: Incident report: treatment works, July 2025
sources.supporting_excerpt: On 14 July 2025 the Lower Basin treatment works dosed chlorine at four times the permitted level for roughly three hours, the utility confirmed.

claims.statement: The Regional Health Office recorded 48 cases of skin irritation at Riverside Clinic between 14 and 17 July 2025.
claims.notes: The office does not link the cluster to the dosing incident.

sources.title: Skin irritation cluster, Eastfield
sources.supporting_excerpt: The Regional Health Office recorded 48 cases of skin irritation at Riverside Clinic between 14 and 17 July 2025.

claims.verification_note: Official count; no link to the dosing is stated.

claims.statement: An anonymous forum user wrote that trucks dump drums into the river every Friday night near Millbrook.

sources.title: Night dumping?
sources.supporting_excerpt: A user who did not give a name wrote that trucks dump drums into the river every Friday night near Millbrook.

claims.verification_note: Anonymous forum post, kept as a weak lead.

claims.statement: The Regional Health Office said 300 people were hospitalised in Eastfield in July 2025.
claims.notes: (A deliberately bad claim: the excerpt is not on the page.)
claims.verification_note: The excerpt is not on the page (the page says 48 cases, not 300 hospitalised). Dropped sources: source 0: not_found, no replacement quote.

claims.statement: The Valley Courier reported that a tank at the Ridgeline Chemical plant at Millbrook released an estimated 40 cubic metres of solvent into the Foo River on 3 March 2024.
claims.notes: The Authority confirms elevated readings, not the volume or the source.

sources.title: Chemical release at Millbrook plant
sources.supporting_excerpt: On 3 March 2024 a tank at the Ridgeline Chemical plant at Millbrook released an estimated 40 cubic metres of solvent into the Foo River.

sources.title: Notice: Millbrook intake, 3 March 2024
sources.supporting_excerpt: The Authority recorded elevated solvent readings at the Millbrook intake on 3 March 2024 and issued a boil notice affecting 12,000 households.

claims.verification_note: Courier and the Authority are independent origins; the Authority confirms readings, not the volume (noted). The Authority confirms elevated readings and a boil notice; the volume comes from the Courier only.

claims.statement: Basin Watch reported that its volunteers counted about 2,300 dead fish along a 9 km stretch of the Foo River below Millbrook on 5 March 2024.
claims.location: Foo River below Millbrook, Upper Basin
claims.figures: Basin Watch: about 2,300 dead fish over 9 km

sources.title: Fish kill below Millbrook
sources.supporting_excerpt: Basin Watch volunteers counted about 2,300 dead fish along a 9 km stretch below Millbrook on 5 March 2024.

sources.title: Dead fish along the river
sources.supporting_excerpt: According to Basin Watch, volunteers counted about 2,300 dead fish along a 9 km stretch below Millbrook.

claims.verification_note: The Courier relays Basin Watch, so one origin, not two.

claims.statement: Ridgeline Chemical said the release was a fraction of the volume alleged and that no fish kill could be attributed to the plant.

sources.title: Statement on the Millbrook incident
sources.supporting_excerpt: Ridgeline Chemical said the release was a fraction of the volume alleged and that no fish kill could be attributed to the plant.

claims.verification_note: Party statement; recorded as a claim by the party.
